// ### Affine builders
//
// The mutable half of the collection story. Every other collection in this
// vocabulary is immutable-by-value, which leaves no way to *build* one: nothing
// can accumulate points, sample a curve into an array, or assemble a mesh. The
// two builder types below fill that gap without giving up value semantics
// anywhere else, because uniqueness is confined to these two types.
// The `unique` modifier is an affine type discipline
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Substructural_type_system).
//
// `unique` is a declaration-site modifier only. A *use* of `List<T>` or
// `Buffer<T>` is never annotated: the type itself carries the affine
// convention, so every pass of a builder value is a move. Only the intrinsic
// builder names `List` and `Buffer` may be declared unique; the compiler
// hard-rejects the modifier on any other type.
//
// Method effects (the compiler's `UniqueTypes` intrinsic table):
//
// | Effect  | Members            | Meaning                                          |
// |---------|--------------------|--------------------------------------------------|
// | observe | `Count`, `At`      | free use; does not invalidate the builder        |
// | mutate  | `Add`, `AddRange`, `Set` | returns the builder - rebind or chain      |
// | consume | `Freeze`           | zero-copy handoff to an immutable `Array<T>`; the builder is invalidated |
//
// Conventions, runtime-checked today (the static affine pass rides the future
// type-checker workstream - see `../docs/affine-types.md`):
//
// - never store a builder in a field (LINT006) or inside another generic
//   container (LINT007);
// - never capture a builder in a lambda;
// - write `Freeze` with parentheses: `xs.Freeze()`;
// - construct with `new List<T>()` / `new Buffer<T>(n)` at concrete element
//   types, or `xs.EmptyList()` where the element type is a type variable;
// - rebind or chain every mutator (`xs = xs.Add(p)`, or
//   `new List<Integer>().Add(1).Add(2).Freeze()`). Use after `Freeze()` throws
//   at runtime.
//
// The backing runtimes are handwritten (`Plato.Intrinsics/PlatoList.cs`,
// `PlatoBuffer.cs`); the compiler maps `List`/`Buffer` to `PlatoList`/
// `PlatoBuffer` and never generates a struct for a unique type.
//
// The bodiless host signatures for these two types live in
// `intrinsics.library.plato`.

// A growable affine builder: append elements, then promote the backing store to
// an immutable Array<T> with Freeze(). (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dynamic_array)
unique primitive List<T>
{ }
